

● The Cat's Quiet Kingdom

  Across the windowsill, the cat reclines,
  a loaf of fur in patches of warm light,
  her amber eyes half-closed in lazy lines,
  dreaming of mice that vanish out of sight.

  She stalks the dust that drifts through morning air,
  a tiny tiger hiding in a box,
  then pounces on a shadow, swift and fair,
  and tumbles, dignified, among her socks.

  At night she prowls the garden, silver-eyed,
  a ghost that slips through hedges, soft and sly,
  and hunts the moon's reflection, pale and wide,
  then curls up on my pillow with a sigh.

  She purrs like distant thunder, low and deep,
  a motor humming secrets to the dawn,
  and when I wake, she's watching me from sleep,
  as if the day were hers to yawn.

  So here's to cats, the masters of their days,
  who nap through storms and rule the house with grace,
  who judge us from their thrones and go their ways,
  and leave us grateful for their fleeting face.

  No dog could ever match their quiet pride,
  no clock could keep the rhythm of their play.
  They ask for little, give their hearts beside
  the hearth, and teach us softly how to stay.

  Purr on, sweet friend.

  Hi!

✻ Sautéed for 14s · done 11:43 AM
